name: Fives and Threes dominoes
description: Fives and Threes is a connecting domino game in which points are scored when the open ends of the layout add up to multiples of three or five. Popular in British pubs and in the British National Dominoes Championship; play is clockwise and the first player or team to reach exactly 61 wins.

history.origins: Fives and Threes is a line domino game from the UK; score when open ends total a multiple of 3 or 5.
timeline: 1985: British National Dominoes Championship started by Keith Masters; game documented in Arthur Taylor's Guinness Book of Traditional Pub Games (1992).

setup.players: Two to four players; four typically play as two against two in partnership.
setup.dealing: Tiles mixed face down; two players draw 7 tiles each, three or four players draw 5 tiles each. Remaining tiles form the boneyard and are out of play (no drawing).
setup.equipment: Double-six domino set; cribbage board recommended for scoring.

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to reach exactly 61 points by making the open ends of the layout total multiples of 3 or 5 (and optionally scoring for chipping out).
rules.gameplay: First hand starter is determined by lot (e.g. each draws a tile, highest starts); in later hands the turn to start passes left. Play is clockwise. Each turn a player adds one tile to an end of the layout, matching the inward end of the played tile to the outward end of the tile it touches; doubles are placed crosswise and count as the total of their pips when at an open end. A player who cannot play must knock and the turn passes. The hand ends when one player chips out (plays their last tile) or all players are blocked; in the four-player partnership game both members of one team must chip out. After each play the two open ends are totalled: if the total is a multiple of 5, 3 or both, the player scores immediately (e.g. 3→1, 5→1, 6→2, 9→3, 10→2, 12→4, 15→8, 18→6, 20→4). Chip-out scores 1 point. First to exactly 61 wins; a score that would exceed 61 is disregarded.
keyRules: Score when open ends total a multiple of 3 or 5 (or both); possible scores 3→1, 5→1, 6→2, 9→3, 10→2, 12→4, 15→8, 18→6, 20→4.
Doubles at an end count as the sum of their pips for scoring.
Cannot draw from the boneyard; must play a matching tile or knock.
First to exactly 61 wins; going over 61 that deal is disregarded and a new hand is played.

strategy.basic: Track which tiles have been played; the player who can count outstanding tiles has an advantage.
strategy.intermediate: Note numbers on which an opponent was unable to play to infer their hand and block scoring opportunities.
strategy.advanced: Valuable tiles that move one scoring position to another: 0-3, 1-4, 2-5, 3-6, double 3, and double 6; use them to set up or deny multiples of 3 and 5.
tips: Doubles at an end count as the sum of their pips; double 5 and a 5 at the other end make 15 (8 points).
In partnership play both members of a team must chip out to end the hand.
